case_title: BIRAPPA & ANR. v. STATE OF KARNATAKA
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.201, s.109 read with Section 34
neutral_facts: The accused, who were relatives of the deceased, were involved in an incident where the deceased was attacked near a temple. The deceased's brother, who was present at the scene, reported the incident to the police after the body was discovered the next day. The prosecution relied heavily on the brother's testimony, which included details about the attack and the discovery of the body. However, the brother's account was questioned due to inconsistencies in his timeline and the delay in reporting the incident. The brother also provided information about the deceased's condition and the location of the body. The prosecution's case was further weakened by the discrediting of the deceased's wife's testimony, who initially supported the prosecution but later recanted her statements. The trial court convicted one of the accused of murder, while the other two were acquitted. The High Court upheld the conviction of one accused and acquitted the third. The Supreme Court, however, overturned the conviction due to the lack of credible evidence and the suspicious nature of the sole witness's testimony.
